humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark plays a dual role: it uses comics and manga panels as raw material ('content') to evaluate general-purpose visual recognition and multilingual translation capabilities, while also introducing a dedicated task ('Conflict@Culture') that targets disciplinary competence in cultural reasoning and contextual analysis of cultural conflicts ('domain').
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Multimodal visual question answering combining comic panel images with textual questions and translation prompts.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Includes background culture identification (Q1, multiple-choice), cultural object detection (Q2, multiple-choice), conflict identification (Q3, binary yes/no), open-ended structural conflict description (Q4), and multilingual translation of comic dialogue across five languages (Q5).

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Specifically scoped to cultural awareness, cultural conflict identification, and translation within comic book frameworks.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates 11 open-source MLLMs including SPHINX, Monkey, MiniGPT-v2, mPLUG-Owl3, LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, LLaVA-OV, InternLM-XC2.5, Llama3.2, Qwen2.5-VL, and InternVL2.

quantitative_metrics.note: Utilizes Accuracy (ACC), a custom composite accuracy (CACC) for joint reasoning dependencies, BLEU, COMET, and BLEURT.

published_after_march_2023.note: Published as an ICLR 2026 conference paper.

summary: This paper introduces C3B (Comics Cross-Cultural Benchmark), a dataset containing 2,220 comic panels and 18,789 QA pairs designed to assess the multimodal cultural awareness of LLMs. By using fictionalized comic scenes where multiple cultures can coexist or conflict within a single frame, the benchmark evaluates models across three progressive tasks: culture-aware object extraction, cultural-conflict detection, and multilingual translation of comic dialogue. The authors perform extensive evaluations on 11 open-source models, highlighting a profound performance gap between current machines and human annotators.
key_findings: Qwen2.5-VL achieved the highest performance across most tasks (e.g., 53.7% ACC on culture identification and 13.2 BLEU on Japanese-English translation). However, all models exhibited severe difficulties in the cultural-conflict description task (Q4), where error propagation from object detection reduced model ACC to near-zero levels. In human-model analysis, human evaluators achieved 100% accuracy on identifying conflicts, far exceeding the 30.8% - 69.2% range of tested MLLMs.
facets_explanation: The reference translations, which make up the vast majority of the dataset's QA pairs, were produced using a multi-agent DeepSeek-R1 pipeline before undergoing manual verification. Correctly identifying the cultures, cultural objects, and conflicts depicted in the comic panels requires background knowledge not contained within the image stimulus itself. Disagreements among the five student annotators during manual verification were resolved through joint review and consensus group discussions, treating divergence as noise to be eliminated.
